Subject: Post-demo: FinTechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation and helpful feedback. Quick written recap + SLO checklist to keep alignment and make the next steps concrete. Attached: fintechco-slo-checklist.xlsx and the demo recording.

High-level performance targets we captured during the demo:
- Streaming capability (token-by-token) for real-time chat flows — initial response start-of-stream latency target: p95 <= 300 ms.
- Non-streaming (batch) generation for short prompts (<= 128 tokens): p95 <= 200 ms.
- Concurrency: support 150 concurrent active users (peak), ~120 QPS sustained across endpoints.
- Throughput: ability to sustain 10k tokens/sec across the instance pool during peak windows; caching and batching expected to reduce cost.
- Stability: <1% error rate during peak; graceful fallback to smaller model variant under overload.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Redwood provides a scoped SLO checklist and proposed test harness by EOD tomorrow (attached).
2) FinTechCo to confirm measurement methodology (external load generator vs. in-app telemetry) and prioritized flows.
3) Schedule 1-week POC in our sandbox with sample traffic (target start: Apr 12).
4) Finalize decision criteria and commercial terms (budget + SLA) by Apr 30.

Please review the attached checklist and reply with any corrections to the numbers above. I'll loop in Aditya (SE) with the technical test plan separately.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: FinTechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks Marissa — adding the technical measurement notes and the specific test cases we'll run for the POC. A few clarifications from the SE side: 

Measurement methodology (recommended):
- Load generation from our sandbox (external egress) to mimic customer latency; parallel in-app telemetry to validate p95/end-to-end.
- For streaming: measure time-to-first-token and steady-state token throughput separately. Time-to-first-token target = p95 <= 300 ms; steady-state throughput target = >= 120 tokens/sec per worker thread (config dependent).
- For short-turn batch calls (<=128 tokens): measure p50/p95/p99 across 1-8 concurrent requests per connection to capture real-world variance.

Test cases we'll include in the POC harness:
- 1:1 chat (streaming) with 150 concurrent active connections, ramp to 200 for stress test.
- Burst test: 2k QPS for 60s to validate autoscaling triggers and fallbacks.
- Long context test: 4k token context to validate memory/kv cache behavior (non-real-time).

I'll attach a lightweight test config to the Drive folder and we can iterate. If you can confirm preferred measurement window (15m vs 5m p95) we'll finalize the harness.

- Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-performance-brief.pdf (PDF)

Subject: Re: Post-demo: FinTechCo performance recap & SLO checklist

Marissa / Aditya — thanks for the thorough write-up. This aligns closely with what our engineering team needs. A few confirmations and one clarification:

Confirmed targets from our side:
- Streaming: time-to-first-token p95 <= 300 ms (critical).
- Short-turn batch (<=128 tokens): p95 <= 200 ms.
- Concurrency: baseline 150 concurrent active users, stress to 200.
- Sustained throughput: 120 QPS across endpoints; allow 20% headroom.

Clarification: on "10k tokens/sec across the instance pool" — that sounds fine as an aggregate target, but we need guidance on how that maps to per-node configs (gpus/worker threads). If you can include an example mapping for 1x A100-80GB and 4x A10 pools that would be helpful for our infra planning.

Decision criteria for us (to be included in the MAP):
- Must meet streaming p95 target for token-start in our sandbox POC.
- Clear plan for degradation: fallback to smaller model variant with <500 ms additional latency in overload scenarios.
- Cost estimate at 120 QPS sustained with 95th-percentile latency targets met.
- Support for SOC-2 evidence and optional VPC Private deployment.

We can confirm the measurement window as 15 minutes p95 for the POC runs. If you can send the POC schedule and test config by EOD Monday (Apr 5) we'll review and lock dates.

Thanks,
Jordan Ellis
Director, Platform Engineering | FinTechCo
jordan.ellis@fintechco.com
